description: Independent space research team led by Saja (ID: saja2011), focused on developing the Water Catalytic Converter (WCC) for deep-space life support systems aboard spacecraft like Orion. Our work integrates bio-nanocomposite coatings and cyclonic fluid dynamics to achieve sustainable, maintenance-free water purification.
summary: Current deep-space water reclamation systems onboard spacecraft like Orion rely on heavy, consumable-dependent filtration assemblies (weighing up to 50 kg) that suffer from bacterial biofilm clogging and mineral scale buildup in microgravity. The Water Catalytic Converter (WCC) introduces an ultra-lightweight, 5 kg self-cleaning pipeline system engineered for a 5-year maintenance-free operational lifecycle. Its interior is lined with a dark brown bio-nanocomposite matrix (64% Liquid Silicon PDMS, 25% Fungal Melanin, 10% Silver Nanoparticles, and 1% Glutaraldehyde cross-linker) that prevents microbial adhesion and eliminates 100% of pathogens upon contact. Operating at a regulated flow rate of 0.15 L/min, internal micro-helical grooves (Spiral Hydro-Guide) generate a cyclonic flow that converts sharp calcium deposits into smooth, non-adherent crystals (Aragonite). Simultaneously, a Photo-Electrochemical Trap utilizes cosmic radiation to excite the Melanin layer, releasing negative electrons (e-) that neutralize escaping silver ions (Ag+) back into stable elemental silver (Ag0). Finally, swept mineral crystals and neutralized dead organic debris are captured downstream by an integrated Magnetic Mineral Trap (Salt Magnet) and an Activated Carbon Polishing Filter, guaranteeing 100% pure potable water while achieving a 90% Mass Reduction and consuming under 3 Watts.
details: How it works: The Water Catalytic Converter (WCC) replaces heavy 50 kg filtration systems on deep-space spacecraft like Orion with a lightweight 5 kg self-cleaning pipeline. Its interior is coated with a dark brown bio-nanocomposite matrix (64% Liquid Silicon PDMS, 25% Fungal Melanin, 10% Silver Nanoparticles, and 1% Glutaraldehyde cross-linker). Operating at 0.15 L/min, internal micro-helical grooves (Spiral Hydro-Guide) create a cyclonic flow that converts sharp calcium scale into smooth, non-adherent Aragonite crystals. Simultaneously, a Photo-Electrochemical Trap uses cosmic radiation to excite the Melanin layer, releasing negative electrons (e-) that neutralize escaping silver ions (Ag+) back into stable silver (Ag0), preventing water toxicity. Finally, swept mineral crystals and dead organic debris are captured downstream by an integrated Magnetic Mineral Trap (Salt Magnet) and an Activated Carbon Polishing Filter. Benefits & Impact: Achieves a 90% Mass Reduction (5 kg vs. 50 kg), eliminates 100% of pathogens, provides +40% ionizing radiation shielding, consumes less than 3 Watts, and operates maintenance-free for 5 years. Creativity & Design Factors: Integrates passive biomimicry (fungal melanin) with cyclonic fluid dynamics to eliminate moving parts, filter replacements, and microgravity clogging. Tools & Resources: Fluid dynamics modeling, chemical mass-balance calculations, NASA technical literature on Orion life support systems, and AI assistance for linguistic formatting
